title: feat(plugin-auth): an SSO sign-in grants the permission set its IdP group is mapped to
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi98qy3EtdY1M87bPE16diw6k)_

Fixes #30967

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：企业 SSO（OIDC / SAML）登录时，IdP 发来的组会按 `sys_idp_group_mapping` 映射授予普通权限集，和 SCIM 共用同一个映射对象、同一道保存门和同一套边界判断；平台管理员用现有的 `set-group-mapping` 门加 `providerId` 保存映射。
- 为什么改：#30967 第 3 项（最后一项），按裁决 A（记录 6718355623）「同一个映射对象，不建第二套模型」，在 #30959 已落地的映射上补 SSO 一半。
- 风险与回滚：只放宽「组 → 普通权限集」；管理员集与组织边界外的集在保存和每次授予时都被拒，没有安全服务时一律不授予；登录不会因为映射失败而失败（只记 error 日志）。回滚即 revert 本 PR，已授予的行带 `sso-group-projection` 标记，可按标记清理。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-group-projection.ts`（登录时读组、匹配、调用共享对账）、`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/idp-group-mapping-admin.ts`（`providerId` 分支与删除即撤销）、`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-group-projection.ts`（抽出共享的准入与对账，SCIM 行为不变）。
- 两分钟验证：`cd packages/plugins/plugin-auth && pnpm exec vitest run src/sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts -t "IdP group is mapped"`，预期 10 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

Item 3 of #30967 (IdP group → permission set on SSO sign-in), the last open item, under maintainer ruling A (record 6718355623): it follows #30959's ruled model, the same `sys_idp_group_mapping` object, no second model. Built on what PR #31443 landed; nothing in it is duplicated.

- **Shared projection, two sources** (`scim-group-projection.ts`). The boundary admission and the reconcile are lifted into `createMappingAdmission(deps, kind)` and `reconcileMappedGrants(engine, { userId, reason, mappingIds }, admits)`; the SCIM projection now calls them (its own behaviour, refusal text and marker are unchanged, and its suite passes unchanged). A `sourceMappings(engine, kind, sourceId)` read and an SSO marker `ssoGroupProjectionReason(providerId)` (`sso-group-projection: provider 'ID'`) are added.
- **The sign-in hook** (`sso-group-projection.ts`, wired in `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts`). `sso({ provisionUser, provisionUserOnEveryLogin: true })`: every sign-in reads `userInfo.groups`, which the provider's own `mapping.extraFields.groups` fills (a string or a list), matches each value against the provider's rows with the SCIM half's matcher (`group_external_id` when the row names one, else exact `group_display_name`), and reconciles the user's grants carrying this provider's marker. A sign-in with no groups desires nothing: it removes only grants this provider made. Writes go through the engine, so the break-glass guard judges them. A failure never fails the sign-in; it is logged at `error` once, naming the consequence and the remedy.
- **The save door** (`idp-group-mapping-admin.ts`). `POST /admin/scim/set-group-mapping` accepts `providerId` in place of `connectionId` (exactly one). The organization is the provider row's `organization_id`; unknown provider → `reference_not_found`, provider with no organization → `rule_violation`, both on `providerId`; SSO off → `503`. The same boundary judgement and the same `503` without a security service. An SSO save applies at each member's next sign-in (`reprojected: false`). `delete-group-mapping` is source-aware: deleting an SSO mapping removes at once the grants its provider made of that set in that organization, unless another of its mappings still names it.
- **The object** (`platform-objects`). `sys_idp_group_mapping.source_kind` gains the option `sso` (`source_id` = the provider id); three field descriptions name both sources; translations for all nine locales (the `en` bundle regenerated, the eight others translated by hand).
- **Route ledger.** The set row's note describes both sources and drops `requires: 'scim'` (the mount is unconditional, and the door now serves SSO with SCIM off); the delete row's note describes the SSO revoke.
- **Tenant-audit census** (`content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`, `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md`). The delete-revoke is one new engine write site (275 → 276); the generated regions are regenerated and the page's prose figures updated to the census. Gate-required, not a behaviour change.

## Tests

New top-level describe in the existing OIDC SSO harness, `sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts` ("an SSO sign-in grants the permission set its IdP group is mapped to"): the real `AuthManager` with the real `sso()` plugin, driven `/sign-in/sso` → a stubbed IdP → `/sso/callback`, on a real ObjectQL engine over better-sqlite3 with the break-glass guard registered, the mapping saved through the door's own function, judged by plugin-security's real `organizationBoundaryFailure`.

1. A mapped group grants the set in the provider's organization, by display name and by external id (a list claim and a string claim).
2. Leaving the group revokes the projected grant at the next sign-in; a grant made by hand stays.
3. CONTROL: an unmapped group grants nothing.
4. CONTROL: a sign-in with no groups claim lands as before, writes nothing to the grant table and logs nothing.
5. A mapping naming an administrator set, or a set outside the organization boundary, is refused at save (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `permissionSet`, `rule_violation`) and stores nothing.
6. A set redefined outside the boundary after its mapping was saved grants nothing at sign-in.
7. With no security service, the save is refused `503`, and a stored mapping grants nothing at sign-in (fail closed).
8. The break-glass guard still refuses through the sign-in: the last administrator's grant is not removed, and the sign-in still lands (one `error` line).
9. Deleting the mapping removes the grants it projected at once.
10. The door names exactly one source; an SSO source must be a provider that belongs to an organization.

Forced test edits: none. The only edit to existing harness code is additive: `TokenShape` gains an optional `claims` member that `idToken()` spreads into the signed claims.

## Acceptance notes

- Group membership changes reach the platform only at a sign-in: an SSO provider pushes nothing between sign-ins, so a user removed from an IdP group keeps the set until their next sign-in through that provider (SCIM is the push channel for prompt revocation). A deleted mapping's grants are removed at once.
- An absent groups claim is read as "no groups": the provider's own earlier grants are removed. A provider whose mapping does not fill `groups` therefore never grants and never removes anything but its own marked rows, of which it has none.
- A set held through any other row (by hand, by SCIM) is not written again; whichever source wrote first owns the row.
- The door's path keeps the `scim` segment while now serving both sources (seat ruling: no `/admin/sso/*` mounts); listed in open questions as a naming note.
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` does not yet describe group mapping (outside this card's file surface); the changeset and the route-ledger notes carry the operator-facing text.
- SAML: the vendor fills `userInfo` from `mapping.extraFields` the same way (SAML attribute values may be lists, which the reader takes); the end-to-end pins drive OIDC only.

## Verification

Head: `70db6d0601c6ca0f3d64750fcd93c9ce95b87a19` (origin/main `8784ccbc` merged in, no rebase).

<details><summary>Red first on main</summary>

The new describe run against the base before any source change: 10 of 10 red (the door refused `providerId` as an unknown field, and no sign-in granted anything).
</details>

<details><summary>Tests on the head</summary>

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts` (plugin-auth): 1 file, 32 passed.
- plugin-auth full suite under the verify lock: Test Files 244 passed (244), Tests 4372 passed, 10 skipped.
- platform-objects full suite: Test Files 120 passed, Tests 1886 passed.
- `tsc --noEmit` for plugin-auth and platform-objects: exit 0. `eslint --no-inline-config` on both packages: exit 0.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build` under the verify lock: exit 0.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablation: each pin goes red when its behaviour is removed</summary>

Each mutation was applied on disk to the source, the describe run, then restored (`git diff HEAD` empty after each).

| Mutation | Red tests |
| :--- | ---: |
| group matcher always matches | 3 |
| sign-in admission always admits | 2 |
| save-time boundary refusal removed | 1 |
| save-time fail-closed (no security service) removed | 1 |
| reconcile removes grants outside the engine's guard | 1 |
| a projection failure fails the sign-in | 1 |
| reconcile ignores the provider marker | 1 |
| `provisionUserOnEveryLogin` off | 2 |
| delete does not remove the projected grants | 1 |

One first run was a no-op (its replacement still contained the anchor, so nothing changed); it was re-run with a mutation that moved the anchor, which went red. It is the "a projection failure fails the sign-in" row.
</details>

<details><summary>Derived gates</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` on the head derived 108 commands; all 108 ran with exit 0, and `--ran` reconciled: 108 derived, 108 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. On the first pass `check-tenant-audit-census` found the new delete-revoke write without a tenant context: it now carries the grant's organization as its tenant, and the census page and ledger counts are regenerated (`tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`) with the page's prose figures updated to match (276 sites; the provable no-context figure stays 3). `check:i18n` and `check:i18n-stale-fill` pass with the regenerated `en` bundle.
</details>
